# Opslane

> Opslane watches errors and session recordings from a web app, investigates the ones worth fixing against the connected repository, and opens a pull request whose build and tests ran in a sandbox. When it cannot fix something it records a reason code. Self-hosted with Docker Compose. Server, worker, agent core, dashboard, and CLI are AGPL-3.0-only; the SDKs and shared types are MIT.

Every page below is plain Markdown in this repository and is published at https://docs.opslane.com. Paths are repo-relative; the published URL drops the `docs/` prefix and the `.md` suffix.

## Start here

- [Introduction](docs-site/src/content/docs/index.mdx): what Opslane is, who it is for, what it is not
- [Run Opslane locally](docs/quickstart/self-host.md): Docker Compose stack, a seeded project, and a first event that ends in `needs_human` without credentials
- [Install the SDK](docs/install.md): React, Vue, and vanilla setup; `setUser` and why anonymous users cost you ranking and friction; environment labels; source-map pointer
- [Connect GitHub](docs/guides/github-app.md): GitHub App or personal access token, permissions, webhook events
- [Source maps](docs/guides/source-maps.md): the Vite plugin, `OPSLANE_SOURCEMAP_KEY`, build diagnostics, verification

## How it works

- [How issues work](docs/guides/issues.md): occurrences vs issues vs affected users, fingerprint inputs, dropped noise, the ranking formula, status groups
- [Friction and session recordings](docs/guides/friction.md): rage clicks and dead clicks, what the analyzer extracts, the five-signed-in-user promotion bar, insight endings
- [Investigation and fix pull requests](docs/guides/fix-prs.md): the three paths to a PR, the impact bar, what the investigator reads, citation validation, ready vs draft
- [What "verified" means](docs/architecture/precision.md): evidence tiers, the ready and draft gates, and what verification does not guarantee
- [Architecture overview](docs/architecture/overview.md): components, trust boundaries, Postgres as the queue
- [Life of an error](docs/architecture/life-of-an-error.md): the pipeline stage by stage

## Configure

- [Environments](docs/guides/environments.md): label resolution, the project default, and limiting automatic error investigation by environment
- [API keys](docs/guides/api-keys.md): `opslane_pk_` ingest keys and `opslane_sk_` source-map keys, minting, rotation, 401 vs 403
- [Slack notifications](docs/guides/slack-notifications.md): incoming webhooks, new-issue alerts, the daily digest

## Trust and privacy

- [Trust and security model](docs/architecture/trust.md): what each external service receives, credential storage, retention, honest gaps
- [Replay privacy and masking](docs/guides/replay-privacy.md): capture defaults, masking classes, server-side scrubbing, retention
- [Source-map privacy](docs/guides/source-map-privacy.md): where uploaded source lives and who can read it

## Reference (checked against source in CI)

- [SDK options](docs/reference/sdk-options.md): every `init()` option with type and default

## Contracts

- [Event API contract](docs/contracts/events.md): the append-only wire rules for `POST /api/v1/events`
- [Notification contract](docs/contracts/notifications.md): subscriptions, delivery timing, and the internal post-triage payload
- [Reliability contract](docs/contracts/reliability.md): machine-checkable properties of the event-to-resolution pipeline
- [Session replay contract](docs/contracts/C4-amendments.md): chunk, pointer, scrub, and retention invariants
- [Action scope contract](docs/contracts/action-scope.md): what environment scoping gates, and what it deliberately does not
